analysis_notes.notes: The dataset for LM2 Torah 46 contains only 1 bechina edge connecting 2 nodes (המניעות וההסתות ופתויים ↔ חומות). Both nodes are assigned to Package 2. The source text is rich in explicit bechina language identifying 7 additional concepts not captured in the dataset. The Torah's core argument revolves around two domains: (1) the positive domain of mesirut nefesh (self-sacrifice) in prayer and charity, and (2) the negative domain of obstacles/walls/doubts that prevent divine service. The Ba'al Shem Tov parable (treasury surrounded by illusory walls) provides the explicit bechina language for the only dataset edge. The remedy described — crying out to God from the depths of the heart — acts as an eitza (cause-effect) bridge between the two packages.
analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror: Package 1 (mesirut nefesh / strong heart) directly mirrors Package 2 (obstacles / spinning heart). The strong courageous heart (לב חזק ואמיץ) is the exact mirror of the spinning/crooked heart (לב סחרחר). Mesirut nefesh (complete self-surrender to God) is the polar opposite of the obstacles/walls/doubts that prevent that surrender.
